source.title: Underestimated Privacy Risks for Minority Populations in Large Language Model Unlearning
source.authors: Rongzhe Wei; Mufei Li; Mohsen Ghassemi; Eleonora Kreačić; Yifan Li; Xiang Yue; Bo Li; Vamsi K. Potluru; Pan Li; Eli Chien

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or garbling; the text includes the paper and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: It evaluates unlearning efficacy using membership-inference privacy leakage, a different measure from the claim’s knowledge-recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: The study measures privacy leakage for PII records after unlearning and compares random, canary, and minority forget sets. It does not test recovery by fine-tuning, activation edits, quantization, or prompting, nor does it measure targeted-knowledge accuracy near chance. The row records the authors’ explicit aggregate statement; detailed condition-level results are in tables.
record.test_reason: The study measures membership-inference privacy leakage (PrivLeak, the MIA AUC gap between unlearned and retrained models) on PII records. It does not measure targeted-knowledge accuracy near chance, and it applies no relearning, activation-edit, quantization or prompting recovery attack. The construct is related but different: distinguishability from retraining, not recovery of hidden knowledge. No version of the claim is tested, so its findings go under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that random-removal evaluations underestimate privacy risk for minority data: at least 20% more leakage in most cases. They call for minority-aware evaluation. They find gradient ascent unstable and utility-degrading, and Langevin Unlearning the best privacy-utility trade-off, with SCRUB also stable.
record.recipe_differences: Uses PII-focused membership-inference auditing across forget-set scenarios; it does not apply the claim’s fine-tuning, activation-ablation, quantization, or prompting attacks.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary across dataset, unlearning method, MIA variant, model scale, and forget-set scenario. The paper also studies forget-set size, unlearning iterations, computational budget, and method hyperparameters.

fits_no_version.finding: Minority-related canaries and minority records show at least 20% higher MIA privacy leakage than random forget sets in most method × attacker × dataset × model combinations, with exceptions for some Llama-2 methods.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random forget-set evaluations underestimate residual privacy leakage for under-represented PII after LLM unlearning.

fits_no_version.finding: After unlearning, PrivLeak often stays close to the No Unlearn value. Examples: GPT-2 Enron-Phone lossMIA, SCRUB 0.167 and CFk 0.190 vs No Unlearn 0.190 (Table 2). Langevin reduces max PL only 0.6–9% vs Noisy No Unlearn (Table 9).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under a fixed small compute budget, heuristic unlearning methods leave the model nearly as distinguishable from retraining as no unlearning, by MIA.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267, 2025
record.problems: The evidence concerns synthetic canaries and PII privacy auditing with membership-inference metrics, not knowledge-recovery attacks. The text reports a fixed random seed of 42; uncertainty estimates are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: The disaggregated results in Tables 2 and 4–20 and figure-based ablations were not entered as separate rows; R1 captures the authors’ explicit aggregate finding, which is the result relevant here. Those tables report separate methods, MIA variants, datasets, models, and hyperparameter conditions.

untested.parts: Near-chance targeted-knowledge accuracy, retained general ability on benchmarks, and resistance to recovery attacks; only MIA distinguishability from a retrained model is measured.
No relearning or fine-tuning recovery attack.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of blocking versus deleting.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, language or in-context recovery.
Langevin Unlearning is compared on the privacy-utility trade-off, but not against the claim's recovery attacks.

missing.what: Per-method PL compared with the No Unlearn baseline, showing that unlearning barely reduces MIA leakage for several methods. This is related evidence, not a test of any version.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' is overridden. An MIA AUC gap versus retraining is not recovery of targeted knowledge, and no recovery attack is applied. The study uses GPT-2 and Llama-2 7B (LoRA) fine-tuned on Enron/ECHR, with a single seed (42) and no uncertainty reported.

versions.untested_parts: Near-chance targeted-knowledge accuracy, retained general ability as specified, and recovery attacks compared with a model that never saw the knowledge.
No small-set fine-tuning or relearning attack.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of access blocking versus deletion.
No prompt-rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context-information recovery test.
No method is tested for resisting the recovery attacks in the claim.

rows.subject: GPT-2 and Llama-2 7B (aggregate across the tested scales)
rows.stage_stated: fine-tuned on PII datasets; unlearning follows
rows.operation_detail: Measured PrivLeak using membership-inference attacks after unlearning; compared minority-related canary and minority forget sets with random forget sets.
rows.measure: PrivLeak (normalized difference in MIA AUC between unlearned and retrained models)
rows.value: At least 20% higher privacy leakage in most cases for minority-related canaries and minority data than for Random
rows.note: Aggregate finding as stated by the authors; the paper also reports disaggregated results in Tables 2 and 4–7. This is an MIA privacy-leakage result, not a test of the claim’s recovery behaviors.
rows.check: The link to none is correct, and 'observed' holds only for the study's own minority-vs-random PL comparison. The value is a percent excess in PL magnitude over Random. 'Most cases' hides exceptions where Canary/Minority PL magnitude is lower than Random: Llama-2 Enron-Phone RL and GA under lossMIA/Min-K% (Table 2), and Llama-2 Enron-Email RL, NegGrad+ and GA (Table 6). The row is not a test of any claim version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
